conclusions: Repaired energy does not establish an incremental R5 benefit: neural and ridge R5 intervals cross zero on both eligible panels; this is inconclusive, not equivalence.
Large secondary R0 ridge increment is consistent with energy helping the weaker sequence baseline substantially more than R5; neither R0_E learner reaches the corresponding R5 absolute score.
The original three-primary family is now complete: few-shot adaptation passes its family interval; inverse compatibility and repaired energy do not.

Recommend one reviewed full-original-training MPNN study within its40USD hard envelope, as a final selected development coverage check. Retain all original results, use fresh matched R5/P/PC heads and fixed-query descriptive table; no independent confirmation or fourth-primary claim.
Do not expand FoldX: the weak R5 increment does not justify its projected65–80USD full-cohort cost compared with the bounded MPNN question. Do not add grids or pool overlapping evidence.

conclusions: Main MLP net R5_PC minus R5 has a negative point estimate with an interval spanning zero; incremental benefit is not established, and neither harm nor equivalence is established.
Context and peptide-only increments, ridge versions and >=50 sensitivity are likewise inconclusive. No additional arm should be selected by the secondary results.

On identical old4449 queries, expanded fitting raises all absolute scores but neural net increment shrinks from+0.018816 to+0.001088 (min20) and context turns negative. This cannot be explained solely by changing the query population, but source coverage, inner selection and stopping changes remain inseparable; fixed-query points have no added intervals.
The earlier balanced-panel small positive point is not supported as a persistent full-cohort net advantage in this fixed recipe. This does not reject all inverse-folding encoders or architectures.

Stop computational search as planned. Retain useful main learned-representation and few-shot findings, all inconclusive descriptor findings and every original-family result. Do not promote this selected overlapping extension as a fourth primary or independent confirmation.

No added ProteinMPNN descriptor is justified as an established improvement to R5 by these data. Prospective independent assay validation remains the next scientific requirement; no new purchases/outreach/studies are authorized by this review.

reasoning: Balanced ProteinMPNN net neural increment +0.018816 has nominal95%[-0.016250,+0.056637], so benefit is not established.
Its positive net point persists under every fixed-eligibility allele/fold deletion; ridge disagrees and remains a mandatory sensitivity.
Energy neural increment +0.014991 has family98.333%[-0.052436,+0.045026]; ridge increment +0.006510 is also inconclusive. This does not earn its substantially higher full-cohort cost.

The cap64 panel constrains source coverage and fitting density. One final complete-training-cohort assessment plus the fixed-query descriptive comparison is scientifically useful at the bounded cost, even if it resolves to no gain.
This selection follows the balanced outcomes; it is neither independent confirmation nor a fourth frozen-tranche primary.
Keep the reviewed CPU scoring recipe and immutable cache. A GPU change would need new kernel/image/parity studies and is not justified here.

decision.stop_rule: This is the one selected full-cohort extension. Preserve and report every frozen result. No additional model search or second descriptor expansion follows its outcomes.

row_density.definition: number of allele/peptide identity rows per inherited peptide cluster; descriptive counts, not effective independent observations

interpretation: Both cohorts cover all75alleles; additional coverage concerns peptide clusters and extra rows within covered clusters.
The row and cluster expansion factors differ; 4.4xrows is not4.4xindependent clusters. Peptide clusters remain related within alleles, so cluster counts are not effective sample size.
The full study changes source/query composition and fitting density together; descriptive metadata cannot identify a causal density effect.
Row-count thresholds are not assay-eligible panels: eligibility additionally needs observed target rankability/nonconstant labels. No labels were read and eligible assay membership is not asserted.
No new significance test, primary hypothesis, model fit, cloud job or inference is introduced.
